- Perseus is bypassing traditional SBIR grant cycles by briefing multiple Pentagon offices, working with Fort Hood's First Cavalry Division for field testing, and building a pipeline of DoD supporters ahead of demo readiness.

# MDA awards X-Bow to develop low-cost interceptor 

 The Missile Defense Agency is targeting a $750K price tag for the LCI weapon. 

 By Mikayla Easley 

 August 19, 2026 

 A static test of a sub-scale SRM design for X-Bow’s MDA interceptor. (Image credit: X-Bow Systems) 

Defense startup X-Bow has been tapped to develop and demonstrate an affordable interceptor for the Missile Defense Agency in late 2027, the company announced Wednesday.

MDA awarded the two-year, $10.9 million contract to the company in July under the agency’s Rapid Response Small Launcher Technology program, moving X-Bow into phase 2 of the Low-Cost Interceptor (LCI) initiative. Like others across the Pentagon, the effort seeks to rapidly build and test an inexpensive defense solution against advanced missile threats — including hypersonic weapons.

“America can’t out-produce today’s threats with yesterday’s supplier base,” X-Bow CEO Jason Hundley said in a statement. “Our new manufacturing technology lets us bring affordable interceptors and rocket motors to the warfighter faster — and this award is a chance to prove it.”

Affordability is the main requirement outlined in MDA’s solicitation for the LCI program, published in 2025. The document notes that the munition should have a unit cost of less than $750,000 in exchange for a “slightly reduced performance rate.”

results.title: US Funds X-Bow's Low-Cost Missile Interceptor Program
results.snippet:
A static test of a subscale solid rocket motor design for X-Bow’s Missile Defense Agency interceptor. Image: X-Bow Systems

Facebook X LinkedIn Reddit WhatsApp Telegram Share via Email Print

The US Missile Defense Agency (MDA) has awarded X-Bow Systems a $10.9-million contract to develop and flight-test its X-Bow Low-Cost Interceptor, designed to provide a cost-effective defense against ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic threats.

X-Bow said producing both the interceptor and its solid rocket motor (SRM) in-house could reduce costs and eliminate reliance on external motor suppliers, helping avoid supply chain bottlenecks.

Awarded under the MDA’s Rapid Response Small Launcher Technology (R2SLT) effort, the contract calls for X-Bow to design, develop, and demonstrate a high-performance SRM through July 2028.

The R2SLT effort supports the MDA’s Low-Cost Interceptor initiative, which seeks to keep interceptor costs as low as $750,000, compared with about $4 million for Patriot PAC-3 interceptors.

## In-House SRM Production

The key to X-Bow’s low-cost approach is its ability to design and manufacture the interceptor’s airframe, SRM, and propellant in-house. The New Mexico-based startup said its additive-manufactured solid-propellant process can accelerate SRM development, allowing motors to be designed and built in days rather than months or years.
